top_categories.workout_context: 7,615ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
121ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Bogota's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At GFNY Bogota, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
7,615ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Bogota. Practice on paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 62 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Bogota. Train it until it feels boring.
62 miles on paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Base fitness for GFNY Bogota. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Low-cadence force work supports 7,615ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Colombian mountain roads with sustained can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Bogota. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for GFNY Bogota's 62 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.altitude: GFNY Bogota includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Altitude: 2,650m at the start, racing above 3,000m — oxygen availability is 73-75% of sea level; Temperature swings: cold starts (8-10C) in the salt mines, mild at valley floor, cold again at summit.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 62 miles of paved colombian mountain roads with sustained climbing at extreme altitude in Zipaquira, Cundinamarca, Colombia.
